recipes.name: Strawberry Cheesecake French Toast
ingredients_raw: 8 slices bread, cut in half diagonally

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 100 degrees F ( 40 degrees C).
Heat mashed strawberries and 1/2 cup white sugar in a saucepan over medium heat.

Whisk water and cornstarch together in a bowl; stir into mashed strawberries. Cook and stir until thickened, about 5 minutes. Reduce heat to low and simmer while preparing remaining ingredients, stirring occasionally.
Whisk milk and eggs together in a bowl; set aside.
Mash cream cheese, remaining 3/4 cup white sugar, and vanilla extract together in a bowl until smooth.

Spread some cream cheese mixture over 1 triangle-shaped piece of bread; top with another triangle-shaped pieced of bread to cover. Repeat with remaining bread and cream cheese mixture to make 8 triangle-shaped sandwiches.
Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat.

Dip cream cheese-stuffed sandwiches into egg mixture, 2 or 3 at a time; place in the skillet. Cook until golden brown on both sides, about 3 minutes per side. Transfer French toast to a baking sheet and place in the preheated oven to keep warm while cooking remaining sandwiches.
Top French toast with warm strawberry glaze and sliced fresh strawberries; sprinkle with confectioners' sugar. Serve with a dollop of whipped cream.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Cheesecake French Toast
raw_recipe.description: Cream cheese-stuffed French toast is served with a sweet and warm strawberry glaze and topped with whipped cream in this decadent breakfast favorite.

video.description: Brunch just got sweeter! Have a strawberry cheesecake treat to start your morning!

review.reviewBody: Thanks for sharing this tasty recipe. I wanted to make something new for breakfast today...and this certainly hit the spot. The entire family loved this, and was easy to make. The only thing I changed was using my griddle for all the toast at a time, rather than 1 at a time in a skillet. A+++

A great stuffed french toast recipe that doesn't need to soak for hours or bake for a long time. Results were fantastic and easy to do all at once on an electric griddle. I used homemade strawberry rhubarb sauce inside the "sandwiches" and served on top. French bread makes big fluffy servings, but regular bread works well also. Very adaptable to any fruit on hand. Thanks for sharing a great idea!

Whole family loved it, including my picky 14 & 11 year old daughters. I used thick slices of egg twist bread, and it held up very well. I kept the slices whole, and not cut diagonally, and didn't spread the filling to the very edges, so no leakage of the filling while cooking. For the strawberry sauce, next time I'll use 1 lb. of fresh strawberries, but keep the rest of the sauce ingredients the same. Based on other reviews, I used confectioner's sugar in the cream cheese filling (1/2 cup), and cinnamon in the egg dip. Also, 4 eggs and 3/4 milk was enough. The pieces cooked beautifully in a cast iron pan. Added Reddi Whip topping for a nice presentation. There was one piece left, and I'm sneaking it right now! Thanks. Pamela, for the great recipe!

This is delicious! I made the strawberry glaze and the filling ahead to streamline morning prep. Also used a large electric skillet and was able to do all the pieces at once. It was the perfect use for my fresh strawberries. Beautiful presentation dusted with confectioners sugar, a few sliced berries and a sprig of fresh mint. Everyone loved it!!!

My family really liked this. I only changed minor things, such as using 4 eggs and 3/4 milk for the dip (and I still had some left over) and I made 12 sandwiches and had plenty of filling. I cooked at 300 degrees on my griddle and I was able to cook them all at the same time, so I didn't use the oven. I cooked them for about 6-8 minutes per side to make sure all of the egg was cooked--I'm not a fan of soggy french toast, but that wasn't a problem.

Delicious and filling, the whole family loved it! Do follow the advice for the filling to use powdered confectioner's sugar instead of granulated sugar, a mixer whips that up nicely into a smooth creamy wonderful filling. And if your block of cream cheese is cold, either leave it out for 30+ mins or expedite that by warming it up on a plate in the microwave for 1 minute 15 seconds. And the strawberry topping is just right. For a little variety, also offer apple/any flavor of preserves/jam.
Two sandwiches per person for hearty appetites!

I followed the recipe for the French toast pretty closely. However I used only three eggs and a half a cup of milk to coat a total of eight pieces and that was plenty as I hate wasting. Although you could use that egg batter and make some scrambled eggs. Also I found a different recipe for the strawberry syrup sauce as I didn't have any cornstarch. You basically can use the same recipe here without cornstarch additionally I put sliced strawberries in between the pieces of bread with the cream cheese. I would like a griddle to do several pieces at one time however I had to do what the suggested and do one piece at a time and storm in a warm oven. You don't need three minutes per side. I also used in artesian bread so is that it was a thicker denser bread

Made this today and it was absolutely delicious and pretty simple to make. I did use powdered sugar with the cream cheese instead of regular and added a little cinnamon to the eggs. I also used Sara Lee artesano bread, but any thicker bread will do. Definitely a show stopper.

I made most of it the night before (to save time). I put together the triangles of bread with the cream cheese spread between two triangles and pre-made the strawberry sauce. (I re-heated it in the morning). It was delicious! Just what we needed for a sweet fix!

Mothers Day breakfast was a hit for my wife and my adult boys. Switch everything to powder sugar. Use Texas toast, for sure. Then you can cook on all five sides flipping with tongs. Next time I'll make the whipped cream and glaze before hand so they can both cool and firm up.
I'm not crazy about sweets but this was right about max for me. Next time I'll orange zest the glaze, or throw in whatever other berries I have around.

Delicious! Be sure to follow the comment tip about using powdered sugar in the cream cheese part rather than granulated that the recipe calls for. Also be sure to bring strawberry sauce to a near boil to make it thick and darker red. If you don’t, it will be thin and watery. Also you don’t need six eggs. I used 4 and it was more than enough.

Amazing! Once in a while we have breakfast for dinner, but that's because none of us eat breakfast. Although keep in mind this recipe is time consuming. SO worth it though! And the "stuffing/filling" out of this world delicious!! The only change I made was the fruit. My family loves strawberries. I in fact do not. I used canned cherries because that's my preference. A+
my favorite french toast recipe. this time, i was out of cream cheese, so I replaced it with a buttercream w/ mild white cheddar, mozzarella, and parmesan. honestly wasn't bad
Amazing! This is a must make. Good for breakfast and breakfast for dinner.

We absolutely loved this! I used powdered sugar instead of regular sugar. I also added a little lemon juice, strawberry flavor and red food coloring to my strawberries. I also used frozen strawberries that I put in the microwave for two minutes first so they were nice and mushy as well as juicy! I added a little vanilla to my eggs and milk then added some extra eggs once I was done dipping on it to make scrambled eggs and made sausage links to go with everything. I made everything dairy casein free! Perfection! Will definitely make it again with strawberries and other fruit!
Outstanding! I made this for brunch for my family. Everyone loved it and went back for seconds. Definitely a keeper!

This was a delicious breakfast/desert dish. The vanilla cream cheese was perfect. The only problem I encountered was that the strawberry sauce overpowered the taste of the cream cheese.
I will definitely make this dish again. I know my grandsons will love it.
Thank you for sharing this recipe.
